:::{#thm-substitution-logic}
#### Replacing a part by an equivalent part

Let $A$ and $B$ be [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent) [propositions](#def-proposition).
Let $F$ be a [proposition](#def-proposition) built from $A$ and other propositions
with [logical connectives](#def-logical-connective),
and let $F'$ be $F$ with $A$ replaced by $B$.
Then $F \equiv F'$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

The truth value of $F$ in a row of its [truth table](#def-truth-table) <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
is computed from the truth values of its parts in that row, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
using the truth table of each connective.
$F'$ is computed the same way,
except that $B$ takes the place of $A$.
$A$ and $B$ have the same truth value in every row, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so each step of the computation gives the same value for $F'$ as for $F$.
So $F$ and $F'$ have the same truth value in every row. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::

:::
